meta.authorization: owner-stated; see Player_Animation_Project/ASSET_AUTHORIZATION.md; granting party and terms not on file

method.chains: pose continuity: last sample of A vs first sample of B, max distance over the tracked points in skeleton space; exact <= 0.003 m (identical keys: authored chain parts), near <= 0.035 m (pose-compatible)
method.confidence: odometry.confidence: high = coverage >= 0.8, accel_rms < 15 m/s^2, not starting airborne, and context or a grounded start; low = coverage < 0.5 (mostly flight or motion carried by the unexported align that no contact reveals); medium otherwise. Heights and travel of low-confidence clips are not authored values
method.contacts: a heel / ball (foot), palm (hand) or knee is in contact while its world speed stays below 0.40 m/s (step velocities at the key rate); runs of the same limb merge; t0/t1 and f0/f1 = first/last sample of the run. Positions are world fwd/side/up at the run's first sample. hands[].surface_up = lowest of palm, middle metacarpal, middle knuckle origins - 0.02 m (bone origins sit inside the hand); supporting = the hand was the path's anchor in the run or the pelvis moved > 5 cm in the world during it
method.entry_exit: speed / vel = mean pelvis world velocity over the first / last 0.2 s; gait by horizontal speed (idle < 0.35, walk < 2.3, run < 3.8, else sprint; bank speeds walk 1.26, run 3.34, sprint 4.24); pose = nearest reference pose (pose_refs) by mean local rotation difference of POSE_BONES + root tilt (yaw removed) + 100 x |root height difference| (1 cm = 1 deg); anchors = the path's anchor on the first / last step
method.head_top: head_top = headb + 0.13 m (rest pose: headb 1.432, brow_mid 1.489)
method.implied: family-specific geometry the clip was authored for, from the contacts: obstacle / ledge top = supporting hand surface heights (and feet / knees landing above 0.3 m), relative to the start support (feet at t = 0); depth = fwd spread of the top contacts (lower bound); landing = end support height; ladder rung pitch = median vertical step between successive same-hand grips; gap = landing contact fwd - takeoff contact fwd around the longest flight. Values are estimates from the contact path, not authored metadata
method.limits: The align (trajectory) channel was not exported, so travel is reconstructed. It is unobservable while no limb touches anything (flights: ballistic assumption) and where the align itself carries the motion with the body posed in place (e.g. a fall loop: a static foot then reads as standing). The contact estimates are sampled at the clip's key rate (10 Hz for most traversal clips), so contact times are +-1 key and heights within ~0.1-0.2 m
method.odometry: contact path: per step k -> k+1 at the clip's key times, each anchor a (foot = rolling sole of heel + ball: vertical from the lowest sole height, horizontal from the lower of the two; palm; knee) implies align velocity -u_a (u_a its skeleton-space velocity) and pelvis world velocity w_a = u_pelvis - u_a. A Viterbi path picks one anchor or none per step minimising sum (|w_a(k) - w_b(k-1)| / dt / 15 m/s^2)^2 * dt/0.1 while supported, (|dw - g T_air| / T / 6)^2 * T/0.1 + 3.0 per 0.1 s over a flight gap (<= 1.2 s), 8.0 per 0.1 s unanchored at either end (<= 1.5 s), anchor costs (hand 1.0, knee 1.2 per 0.1 s; foot ((|y| - 0.10) / 0.20)^2 per 0.1 s; a foot or knee may anchor only while its sole / joint height is within 0.20 m of its lowest height over +-0.3 s, knees only below 0.25 m: swinging or tucked limbs cannot anchor), a co-stationarity bonus (-1.5 per 0.1 s for an anchor whose skeleton velocity matches another limb's within 0.15 m/s for >= 0.4 s: both planted), a switch cost of 1.0 and contact physics (supported: centre-of-mass a_y >= -g - 3.0, feet / knees |a_h| <= 1.2 (a_y + g) + 3.0; excess costs (excess / 2.0)^2); smoothness and ballistic checks use an approximate centre of mass (COM_W). Flight gaps cost only the part of the landing velocity change that no upward, friction-bounded impact impulse explains, and fly ballistically from the takeoff step; an unanchored start holds the first anchored velocity, an unanchored end extrapolates ballistically. The sequence is padded with up to 1.0 s of context on each side (odometry.context): the clip itself when it loops, an exact pose chain, an ambient enter / loop / exit name set (boundary poses within 0.15 m after a yaw + translation alignment), a graph succession (end-of-clip transition records, boundary poses within 0.15 m), a near pose chain, or a locomotion loop (LOOPS) at the phase whose legs / pelvis / head are within 0.10 m; neighbours are joined with a 0.2 s cross-fade of the boundary offset. A clip without preceding context gets a soft entry prior: its first anchored centre-of-mass horizontal velocity costs (|v - v_gait| / 1.5 m/s)^2 with v_gait forward at the entry gait's bank speed implied by the name (odometry.context.entry_prior_speed; sprint 4.24, run 3.34, walk 1.26, idle / ladder / ledge / hang 0). The world origin is still the clip's own first sample. No align rotation is modelled: travel.yaw_change_deg is the skeleton-space facing change and odometry.planted_yaw_drift_deg flags planted feet that rotate (an align turn)
method.part: variant clips (weapon parts, --hands, --add): keyed bones, length vs base, and the hand contacts of the composite pose (base with the part's keyed bones replaced; additive clips are not composed) using the base clip's align path
method.root_motion: The rig has no ground-level root bone (ground_root_bone false): its `root` bone is the hips (pelvis height), and the game's align / trajectory channel was not exported. root_motion.root_* = that bone's horizontal travel in skeleton space (start -> end, and the largest excursion); in_skeleton = the hips themselves travel >= 0.5 m and at least half the contact-derived world travel (the clip carries its travel in the skeleton instead of the align). World travel always comes from the contacts (odometry), which covers both cases

units.frame: world = the clip's align frame at its first sample (the character's start position): fwd = +Z, side = +X (left), up = +Y; skel = skeleton space (the moving, unexported align)
